senses.gloss: m. (σάγος, sagus, sagum) a coarse woolen blanket, mostly mentioned as a mattress to sleep on.
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 277:3">Sifré Deut. 277</cite> <he>ס׳ בלילה וכ׳</he> he must give him back the sagum for the night (<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 9:13">B. Mets. IX, 13</cite> <he>את הכַּר</he>). Sifré ib. 234 (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:12">Deut. XXII, 12</cite>, ‘wherewith thou clothest thyself’) <he>פרט לס׳</he> this excludes the sagum.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 29:1">Kel. XXIX, 1</cite>. Ohol. XI, 3; a. fr.—Pl. <he>סָגוֹסִין</he>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 7:1">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. VII, 1</cite> (ed. Zuck. <he>סגסגין</he>, oth. ed. <he>סגסין</he>, (corr. acc.; v. R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 29:1">Kel. XXIX, 1</cite>). Ib. V, 11 <he>הסנסין</he> (corr. acc.; v. R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 28:8">Kel. XXVIII, 8</cite>); <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 28:8">ib.</cite>

<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 5:14">Neg. V, 14</cite> <cite ref="O01246"><he>סנסון</he></cite> (corr. acc.).—[Tanḥ. ed. Bub., Vayera 21 <he>הוא מהלך בסגן</he> Ms. R. (Ms. Parma <he>בסגו</he>, printed text <he>פגן</he>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 50">Gen. R. s. 50</cite>, a. e. <he>כפגן</he>) read: <he>מהלך בסָגוּן כפגן</he> he travelled in a sagum like a commoner; (v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Sagum.]
